Definition: guilt; by implication, a fault; also a sin-offering
BiblicalUsage: The guilt offering is the offering for the sin a man did not mean to do, and for the sin he did not know he did. If a soul commit a trespass through ignorance, he shall bring a ram for a trespass offering; Isaiah says thou shalt make His soul an offering for sin, and He shall see His seed; and the Philistines are told to return the ark with a trespass offering, lest His hand be not removed from them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the guilt offering is the most merciful part of the law, because it covers the sin you did not know you did: ignorance is no excuse, but it is not beyond atonement either. And Isaiah takes the offering and lays it on the Servant, whose soul is made the offering for sin, and I hold that there is the whole gospel, that Christ was made the guilt offering for the sins we never even knew we committed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
